summary: 10-yr change (ft), 2014 fold (trained on water levels through 2014, weather climatology through 2013; n = 695 wells): model MAE 6.13 / RMSE 9.98 / bias -5.10; no-change MAE 6.25 / RMSE 9.58 / bias +4.83; own-trend MAE 7.42 / RMSE 11.99 / bias -6.66; county-trend MAE 7.80 / RMSE 11.10 / bias -7.00. The model beats no-change on MAE only, marginally, and loses on RMSE: it forecast a mean change of -9.9 ft against -4.8 ft observed, because declines slowed after 2014. Held-out wells (spatial, re-fitted without them): model MAE 6.64 / RMSE 10.44 / bias -5.77 vs no-change MAE 5.94 / RMSE 9.54 / bias +4.61 (model does not beat no-change). 80% intervals covered 91% (temporal) and 89% (spatial). The clear win is the 2004 fold, where declines sped up: temporal model MAE 6.65 / RMSE 12.12 / bias +4.42 vs no-change MAE 12.20 / RMSE 19.46 / bias +11.83; spatial model MAE 7.60 / RMSE 13.30 / bias +5.42 vs no-change MAE 13.21 / RMSE 20.26 / bias +12.98.

saturated_thickness_vs_usgs_2009.note: Our 2009 surface = 2009 winter level minus base at each well (KGS pick or USGS OFR 98-393 + KGS residual), kriged with a quadratic drift. USGS SIR 2012-5177 used its own water-level surface and the Gutentag et al. base and set <=10 ft cells to 10 ft, so cells with published <=10 ft are excluded.

grace_vs_wells.notes: Wells: aquifer-area-weighted mean winter water-level change chained from county means, times specific yield 0.15 (range 0.10-0.20), over the 89% of the region underlain by the aquifer. Annual correlation with GFZ GRACE/GRACE-FO total water storage r = 0.86 (year-to-year changes r = 0.49). Both show the same drought drawdowns, but the well-based storage loss 2003-2026 (-4.0 cm/yr) is about 4x the GRACE trend (-0.9 cm/yr) at Sy 0.15 (about 6x at Sy 0.20 and 3x at Sy 0.10). Reported gross pumping (WIMAS 2016-2025, 2.04 million AF/yr) equals 4.2 cm/yr over the region; net depletion is smaller (return flow, recharge) but the same order as the well-based number. A likely (untested) reason for the gap is GRACE's footprint of a few hundred kilometres, which mixes this concentrated loss with a larger area that includes non-irrigated land (signal leakage) as well as neighbouring areas that are also losing water, so leakage alone may not explain it. GRACE is therefore used as an independent check of timing and sign, not as a volume constraint. Since GRACE-FO (2018-2026) the gap narrows: wells -3.3 vs GRACE -2.2 cm/yr.
